name: delay
prose: Busy-waits for roughly usecs microseconds using the Open Firmware millisecond counter: it computes msecs = usecs / 1000 (C integer division, truncating toward zero, so 1500 microseconds waits 1 ms and a negative or sub-millisecond value gives a wait of 0 or less), records start = OF_milliseconds(), and loops, polling OF_milliseconds(), until OF_milliseconds() - start is no longer less than msecs. It returns nothing, and for msecs <= 0 the loop ends at its first test.
note: ofw_time.c:50-58 read in full. Reviewers: round 1 (waits only floor(usecs/1000) ms, not at least usecs microseconds) right; round 15 (a negative usecs waits zero, so floor is the wrong word) right, 54 and 57. Tally 2 right.

name: getopt
prose: Boot-loader getopt: returns the next option letter from nargv according to the option string ostr, -1 when there are no more options, '?' (BADCH) for an unknown option or a missing argument (or BADARG ':' for a missing argument when ostr starts with ':'). It uses the globals optind, optreset, opterr, optopt and optarg and a static scan pointer place. When optreset is set or the current word is exhausted it restarts at nargv[optind]: if optind >= nargc or the word does not begin with '-' it returns -1; a word "--" advances optind and returns -1. It takes the next letter into optopt; if it is ':' or not found in ostr it advances optind when the word is finished and returns BADCH (printing a message when opterr is set and ostr does not begin with ':'), except that a letter '-' (a lone "-") returns -1 without advancing. For a letter that takes no argument it sets optarg to NULL and advances optind at the end of the word; for one that takes an argument it sets optarg to the rest of the word, or to the next argv word, or, when none is left, returns BADARG or BADCH as above; optind advances past the argument. On success it returns the option letter.
note: getopt at getopt.c:48-101, read in full. Reviewer round 1 (the code returns -1 for '-' not in ostr, not BADCH) right, 71-72. Tally 1 right.

name: gptbootconv
prose: Converts "boot once" GPT partition entries of the table described by hdr into "boot failed" entries and writes the changes back; which names the table (primary or backup) for messages, dskp the disk, and the function returns nothing. It computes entries per sector as DEV_BSIZE / hdr_entsz and walks only the complete sectors of the table (hdr_entries / entries_per_sec sectors; a trailing partial sector of entries is not visited when the entry count is not a multiple). For each entry whose attribute bits, masked to BOOTME, BOOTONCE and BOOTFAILED, equal exactly BOOTONCE (other attribute bits are not considered), it clears BOOTONCE and sets BOOTFAILED. Each sector that contained a changed entry is copied to the scratch buffer secbuf and written with drvwrite (a failure prints a message and the loop goes on). If any entry changed it recomputes the table CRC and the header CRC (with the table CRC stored first), copies the header into a zeroed sector and writes it to hdr_lba_self with drvwrite (a failure prints a message). If no entry changed it returns without writing anything.
note: slice cut the head; real function gptbootconv at gpt.c:232-279, read in full. Reviewers: original (converts entries whose masked flags equal BOOTONCE, not attributes exactly equal to BOOTONCE) right, 248-251; round 15 (entries in a trailing partial sector are omitted) right, 243. Tally 2 right.

name: pkg_seek
prose: Seek method of the package (tar) file system; f is the open file (f_fsdata a struct tarfile), ofs the offset and whence one of SEEK_SET, SEEK_CUR and SEEK_END; it returns the resulting file position tf_fp or -1 with errno set. It returns -1 with EBADF if f_fsdata is NULL, and with EINVAL for any other whence. It computes the signed distance delta to move (from tf_fp for SEEK_SET, ofs itself for SEEK_CUR, relative to the end for SEEK_END). A backward move is allowed only when the data is cached: if tf_cachesz > 0 and tf_fp <= tf_cachesz and the new position is not negative it sets tf_fp to the new position and returns it; in every other backward case (no cache, tf_fp beyond the cache, or a negative target) it returns -1 with ESPIPE. A forward move reads and discards data with pkg_read in chunks of at most 512 bytes until delta is used up or the end of the file is reached; an error from pkg_read is stored in errno and -1 returned. It returns tf_fp, which can be less than the requested position when the end of the file is reached first.
note: slice cut the head; real function pkg_seek at pkgfs.c:344-400, read in full; pkg_read not read. Reviewers: original (omits EBADF for a NULL f_fsdata and the propagation of pkg_read errors) right, 354-357 and 392-395; round 15 (ESPIPE also when tf_fp > tf_cachesz or the cache is empty, not only when the target precedes the cached data) right, 376 and 385. Tally 2 right.

name: kvprintf
prose: Formats fmt with the arguments in ap, sending each output character either to the callback func (called with the character and arg) or, when func is NULL, into the buffer pointed to by arg, and returns the number of characters produced (retval); no NUL terminator is added by this function and the caller must provide a buffer large enough for the whole output. A NULL fmt is replaced by "(fmt null)\n", and a radix below 2 or above 36 is replaced by 10 (the radix is used for %r and %R conversions). The format is scanned character by character: ordinary characters are output; after '%' the flags and modifiers ('#', '+', '-', '0', '.', '*', digits, h, hh, j, l, ll, q, t, z) are accumulated and the conversion is one of b (bit-field print), c, D (hex dump), d, i, n, o, p, r, s, S (16-bit wide string), u, X, x, y, or "%%". Numbers are taken with the size given by the modifiers, converted in the proper base with sign, '#' prefix, padding and precision, and written with left or right adjustment; %s prints "(null)" for a NULL pointer and honours the precision; %n stores the count so far through a pointer of the size selected by the modifiers. A conversion character that is not recognised outputs the text of the directive from its '%' up to and including that character and then sets stop, after which the rest of the format string is output verbatim (the directive arguments are not consumed). The function returns retval when it reaches the NUL at the end of the format.
note: slice cut the head; real function kvprintf at printf.c:238-577, read as a control-flow outline (the per-conversion bodies and the number formatting were skimmed, not read line by line: partly read). Reviewer round 15 (the unknown-directive path emits only '%' and the directive up to the unknown character, not the remainder verbatim) partly right: the remainder is then output verbatim because stop is set (554-566, 280). Tally 1 mixed.

name: zfs_bootenv
prose: Rebuilds the boot-environment menu for the ZFS dataset name; it sets environment variables and returns 0 on success or an error number. It returns EINVAL if name is NULL or the variable zfs_be_root is unset, and ENOMEM if replacing zfs_be_root with name fails (zfs_be_root is overwritten before the pool lookup, so a later failure leaves it changed). It then empties the list zfs_be_head and the count and splits name into a pool name and dataset name (EINVAL if that fails), finds the pool (ENXIO if unknown), looks up the dataset (returning the lookup's error) and calls zfs_callback_dataset with zfs_belist_add to collect the boot environments; the result of that callback is kept as the return value. It computes the number of pages, stores it in zfs_be_pages (ENOMEM on failure, without freeing the list), parses zfs_be_currpage with strtol (which requires the variable to be set) and resets it to "1" if it exceeds the page count (ENOMEM on failure, again without freeing the list). It calls zfs_set_env() (its result is ignored) and frees all collected entries, then returns the result of the callback. The list is therefore leaked on the ENOMEM returns after the callback and on the early error returns after it was initialised.
note: zfs_bootenv at zfs.c:1869-1928, read in full; zfs_set_env, zfs_belist_add not read. Reviewers: original (zfs_set_env result ignored, so the menu variables may not be set) right, 1917; round 2 (the list is not freed on the ENOMEM returns) right, 1906-1913; round 15 (zfs_be_root is overwritten before the split and lookup, so the errors leave it changed) right, 1883-1886. Tally 3 right.

name: sys_sigreturn
prose: System call that restores the user context saved by a signal handler frame; uap->sigcntxp points to the user-space ucontext_t and the function returns EJUSTRETURN on success or an errno. It copies the context in (returning the copyin error), returns EINVAL if mc_flags has bits outside _MC_FLAG_MASK, if the new rflags are not EFL_SECURE with respect to the current ones, or if the ss or cs selector fails is_seg_val. If the code segment is not CS_SECURE it posts SIGBUS (BUS_OBJERR, T_PROTFLT, at the current rip) with trapsignal and returns EINVAL, so the thread's signal state is changed on that path. When _MC_HASFPXSTATE is set it returns EINVAL if the extended state length is too large, allocates a save area and copies the user's extended state in (freeing the area and returning the copyin error on failure); otherwise there is none. It then calls set_fpcontext and frees the area, returning its error if non-zero. Only after all of those checks pass does it copy the general registers into the trapframe, update the pcb's fs and gs bases, with COMPAT_43 set or clear SS_ONSTACK from mc_onstack, set the signal mask from uc_sigmask with kern_sigprocmask, and return EJUSTRETURN. Any earlier error return leaves the trapframe, bases and signal mask unchanged.
note: sys_sigreturn at exec_machdep.c:261-369, read in full; set_fpcontext and update_pcb_bases not read. Reviewers: original (the CS_SECURE failure posts SIGBUS via trapsignal, so thread state is not unchanged) right, 314-323; round 15 (the precondition of a readable context and clean mc_flags is not needed, since the code handles copyin failure and bad flags with errors) right, 277-288. Tally 2 right.

name: hammer_time
prose: First C function of the amd64 kernel, called once on the boot CPU from locore with modulep (the preload metadata) and physfree (the first free physical address after the loaded kernel and modules); it sets up CPU identification, descriptor tables, per-CPU data, consoles, memory and thread0, and returns the top of thread0's kernel stack (thread0.td_md.md_stack_base) for the assembly caller to switch to. In order it: records the boot-method flags and the BIOS warm-boot word, identifies the CPU and any hypervisor, initialises the CPU caches, reads the PTI, PCID, XSAVE and scheduler tunables, relocates ifuncs, links proc0 and thread0, zeroes the thread0 kernel stack, builds and loads the GDT, sets the FS/GS base registers, initialises the dynamic per-CPU area and the BSP pcpu, initialises the mutexes, fills the IDT with the exception vectors (using the PTI variants when pti is set) and loads it, reads the CPU-mitigation tunables, finishes CPU identification, initialises clocks, the CPU registers, the IST stacks, the task register and the fast system call MSRs, and sets thread0's top of stack. It reads the debug.late_console tunable: when it is not set it initialises the console (cninit) and the kernel debugger (amd64_kdb_init) before sizing memory, and when it is set it does both later (cninit before the PCI quirks and amd64_kdb_init after the interrupt controller setup), so the debugger is initialised on both paths. It then calls getmemsize and init_param2, sets up the interrupt controller, msgbuf and FPU, selects the user segment selectors, loads the data segment registers, clears thread0's pcb flags, copies the "kernelname" environment value, calls the sanitizer and optional FDT initialisers and returns thread0.td_md.md_stack_base.
note: slice cut the head; the real function hammer_time at machdep.c:1301-1633, read as a control-flow outline (call sequence and conditions; the many setidt and tunable lines only summarised: partly read). Reviewer round 17 (amd64_kdb_init runs only when !late_console) wrong: line 1587-1588 runs it when late_console is set. Tally 1 wrong.

name: cpu_minidumpsys
prose: Writes an amd64 minidump through the dumper device di; state supplies the msgbuf pointer and the dump bitset; it returns 0 on success or a positive error number. It walks the kernel page tables from km_low up to the kernel virtual-memory end: for every valid 1 GB or 2 MB mapping it adds each dumpable physical page of the mapping to the dump bitset (vm_phys_is_dumpable, vm_page_dump_add), for page-table pages it adds the page-table page itself and every valid 4 KB mapping whose physical address is in the direct map and dumpable, and it counts the size of the page-directory pages that will be written (pmapsize). It then totals the dump size (pmap pages, msgbuf, dump_avail, the bitmap and one header page) and, going through the bitset, adds PAGE_SIZE for each page that is in the direct map and dumpable and removes (vm_page_dump_drop) the others. It fills a minidump header (magic, version, sizes, KERNBASE, direct map range), starts the dump with dump_start and writes in order: the header page, the msgbuf, the dump_avail array, the bitmap, the page-directory pages (a zero page for an invalid 1 GB entry, a synthesised directory for a 1 GB mapping, the real directory page when it is dumpable, otherwise a zero page; each followed by blk_flush), then every page in the bitset, then flushes and calls dump_finish. Any failing step goes to the fail path, which makes a negative error positive; for ENOSPC it retries the whole dump from the start up to dump_retry_count times, for ECANCELED it reports that the dump was aborted, for E2BIG it reports the size needed, and it returns the error.
note: slice cut the head; real function cpu_minidumpsys at minidump_machdep.c:162-415 (the name minidump_dump does not exist), read in full. Reviewer round 17 (the page-table walk does not mark the bitmap; the code only writes page-directory pages and drops undumpable entries) is wrong: the first walk marks pages with vm_page_dump_add at 207-252, in addition to the later writing and dropping at 262-269 and 326-374. Tally 1 wrong.

name: pmap_pkru_update_range
prose: Sets the protection-key (PKRU) field of the page-table entries covering [sva, eva) of pmap to keyidx; the caller must hold the pmap lock (asserted), pm_type must be PT_X86 and keyidx at most PMAP_MAX_PKRU_IDX (both MPASS). It walks the range one top-level region at a time: an invalid PML4 or PDP entry is skipped; a 1 GB mapping gets its key field replaced if it differs, with a KASSERT that the mapping is not partially covered (va_next <= eva); an empty page-directory entry is skipped; a 2 MB mapping whose whole span lies in the range gets its key field replaced, while a partially covered 2 MB mapping is first demoted with pmap_demote_pde (if the demotion fails that region is skipped); and for the 4 KB mappings in the remaining span each valid page-table entry gets its key field replaced if it differs. Whenever any entry was changed it calls pmap_invalidate_range(pmap, sva, eva) once at the end. It returns nothing; the wrap-around of va_next is clamped to eva.
note: pmap_pkru_update_range at pmap.c:11556-11644, read in full; pmap_demote_pde and pmap_invalidate_range not read. Reviewer round 1 (omits the KASSERT precondition that a 1 GB mapping must not be partially covered) right, 11590-11593. Tally 1 right.

name: pmap_ts_referenced
prose: Counts and clears (where safe) the reference bits of the mappings of the managed page m (asserted not VPO_UNMANAGED) across all pmaps, and returns cleared + not_cleared: the number of mappings found referenced whose bit was cleared plus those found referenced whose bit could not be cleared, so the result can be non-zero when no bit was actually cleared. It takes the page's PV list lock as a write lock itself and releases it before returning (the caller must not hold it). It scans the 2 MB mappings on the page's pv list and then the 4 KB mappings on m's own pv list, locking each pmap (if the trylock fails it drops the PV lock, takes the pmap lock and restarts the scan when the lists changed). For each mapping it marks the page dirty if the entry is both modified and writable; if the referenced bit is set it clears it with atomic_clear_long and invalidates the page when safe_to_clear_referenced allows it, and counts it as cleared; for a 2 MB mapping it clears the bit only for a limited subset of mappings (selected by a hash of the physical address, virtual address and pmap) that are not wired, demoting or removing the 4 KB mapping when it is not safe to clear, and otherwise counts it as not cleared; for a 4 KB mapping that cannot be cleared safely and is not wired it removes the mapping (counted as cleared), and a wired one is counted as not cleared. Visited pv entries are rotated to the tail of their list. The scan stops once cleared + not_cleared reaches PMAP_TS_REFERENCED_MAX (the test is applied after counting, to either kind of count) or when all entries have been visited. It then frees any page-table pages collected and returns the sum.
note: pmap_ts_referenced at pmap.c:8946-9141, read in full except the comment lines (9002-9019, 9029-9036 etc.); the helpers (safe_to_clear_referenced, pmap_demote_pde_locked, pmap_remove_pte) not read. Reviewers: round 1 (returns not_cleared when no bits were cleared, not just a count of cleared bits) right, 9140; round 2 (the stop condition is on found counts, not only cleared ones) right, 9071 and 9135-9136. Tally 2 right.

name: pmap_change_attr
prose: Changes the memory (cache) attribute of the kernel virtual range [va, va + size) to mode: it takes the kernel_pmap lock, calls pmap_change_props_locked(va, size, PROT_NONE, mode, MAPDEV_FLUSHCACHE), releases the lock and returns that function's result (0 on success, or an error number such as EINVAL or ENOMEM produced by pmap_change_props_locked, which was not read; the values are positive errno numbers, not negative ones).
note: pmap_change_attr at pmap.c:9663-9672, read in full; pmap_change_props_locked not read, so the exact error cases and the overflow condition mentioned in the old prose are not verified. Reviewer (the old formal contract used negative errno values but the code returns positive ones) right, contract removed.

name: pmap_change_prot
prose: Changes the protection of the kernel virtual range [va, va + size) to prot: it returns EINVAL without changing anything if va is below kva_layout.km_low; otherwise it takes the kernel_pmap lock, calls pmap_change_props_locked(va, size, prot, -1, MAPDEV_ASSERTVALID), releases the lock and returns that function's result (0 on success, or an error number produced by the callee, which was not read; positive errno values).
note: pmap_change_prot at pmap.c:9682-9695, read in full; pmap_change_props_locked not read. Reviewer (the code returns positive EINVAL and the helper can also return an error) right, contract removed.

name: read_rflags
prose: Static inline function returning the current RFLAGS register as a u_long: it executes "pushfq; popq %0" in volatile inline assembly, which pushes the flags on the stack and pops them into a register, and returns that value. The stack pointer is temporarily changed by the pushfq/popq pair, which is restored by the pop; there is no other effect on memory. On x86-64 the upper 32 bits of RFLAGS are reserved and read as zero and bit 1 reads as 1 (an architectural property, not enforced by this code).
note: slice cut the head; real function read_rflags at cpufunc.h:269-275, read in full. Reviewer round 15 (pushfq/popq touch the stack, contradicting "no memory affected") right; reviewer round 1 (formal contract weaker than prose) moot, contract removed.

name: systrace_args
prose: Generated DTrace helper systrace_args(sysnum, params, uarg, n_args): it fills the 64-bit array uarg with the arguments of the Linux system call sysnum read from the matching args structure params, and sets *n_args to the argument count; it returns nothing. It is one large switch with a case per system call number: each case casts params to that call's args structure, stores the arguments in order into slots uarg[0], uarg[1], ... and sets *n_args. Integer-typed and unsigned-typed arguments (int, l_uint, l_ulong, l_size_t and similar) are stored through the int64_t alias iarg (sign-extending per the field type), and pointer arguments are stored through uarg as (intptr_t) values. A system call without arguments, and some calls whose case does not store its arguments, only set *n_args (to 0 for the no-argument calls). A sysnum with no case reaches the default branch, which sets *n_args to 0 and writes nothing to uarg; params is not read in that case. (This slice covers the cases for system call numbers from the middle of the switch in the amd64 Linux table.)
note: slice cut the head; the real function is systrace_args at linux_systrace_args.c:9-2819 (the name syscall-arg-decode-switch does not exist), read at its head (9-30) and its tail with the default case (2811-2819); the bulk of the cases were not read individually ("partly read"). Reviewer round 17 (the default case sets *n_args = 0, not unmodified) right, 2816-2818. Tally 1 right.

name: systrace_entry_setargdesc
prose: Generated DTrace helper (the real name is systrace_entry_setargdesc, at linux_systrace_args.c:2821-7306) that writes the type description of argument number ndx of Linux system call sysnum into the buffer desc of size descsz; it returns nothing. Only when p is non-NULL it copies it with strlcpy(desc, p, descsz) (truncated and NUL-terminated to fit descsz); otherwise desc is left unchanged. The slice region contains the cases for calls around number 441 (with arguments 0 to 5) and the empty cases for the later numbers up to 453.

name: pci_docfgregread
prose: Reads a PCI configuration register for (domain, bus, slot, func, reg) with the access width bytes and returns it as a uint32_t. If domain and bus are both 0 and bit slot of pcie_badslots is set (slot must be below 32 for the shift to be defined) it uses the legacy I/O-port method pcireg_cfgread. Otherwise, if cfgmech is CFGMECH_PCIE and pcie_lookup_region finds a memory-mapped region for the domain and bus, it returns pciereg_cfgread on that region. Otherwise, for domain 0 it uses the legacy pcireg_cfgread, and for any other domain it returns -1, which as a uint32_t is 0xFFFFFFFF whatever the width. pcireg_cfgread takes and releases the pcicfg_mtx spin mutex, so the caller must not hold it on the legacy paths.
note: pci_docfgregread at pci_cfgreg.c:114-132, read in full. Previous prose unreviewed; consistent with the code.

name: pci_cfgregread
prose: Public read of a PCI configuration register. If reg is PCIR_INTLINE and bytes is 1 it reads the value with pci_docfgregread and returns PCI_INVALID_IRQ (255) when it is 0 or at least 128 (this includes an all-ones failure value), otherwise the value read. For every other register and width it returns pci_docfgregread(domain, bus, slot, func, reg, bytes) unchanged (so a failed access yields 0xFFFFFFFF as in pci_docfgregread). The caller must not hold pcicfg_mtx on the legacy paths.
note: pci_cfgregread at pci_cfgreg.c:135-147, read in full. Previous prose unreviewed; consistent.

name: pci_cfgregwrite
prose: Public write of a PCI configuration register (domain, bus, slot, func, reg) with data of width bytes; it returns nothing. If domain and bus are both 0 and bit slot of pcie_badslots is set (slot below 32) it writes with the legacy method pcireg_cfgwrite (which takes and releases the pcicfg_mtx spin mutex) and returns. Otherwise, if cfgmech is CFGMECH_PCIE and a memory-mapped region covers the domain and bus, it writes through pciereg_cfgwrite (this path does not take pcicfg_mtx in this function) and returns. Otherwise it uses pcireg_cfgwrite for domain 0, and for any other domain does nothing.
note: pci_cfgregwrite at pci_cfgreg.c:150-169, read in full. Reviewer round 1 (the MCFG path does not acquire pcicfg_mtx internally) right.

name: pci_cfgenable
prose: Prepares the legacy PCI configuration mechanism 1 for an access and returns the data port to use, or 0 if the arguments are invalid. When bus <= PCI_BUSMAX, slot <= PCI_SLOTMAX, func <= PCI_FUNCMAX, reg lies in 0..PCI_REGMAX, bytes is not 3 and at most 4, and reg is aligned to the width (reg & (bytes - 1) is 0; for bytes 0 that requires reg == 0), it writes the enable word (bit 31, bus, slot, function and the register number with its low two bits cleared) to CONF1_ADDR_PORT with outl and returns CONF1_DATA_PORT plus the low two bits of reg. In every other case it writes nothing and returns 0. It takes no locks; the callers hold pcicfg_mtx.
note: pci_cfgenable at pci_cfgreg.c:172-185, read in full. Reviewer round 1 (a negative reg returns 0) right: reg is compared as unsigned (175).

name: pcireg_cfgread
prose: Reads a configuration register with the legacy I/O-port mechanism and returns it as an int. It takes the pcicfg_mtx spin mutex, calls pci_cfgenable, and if that returned a non-zero port reads 1, 2 or 4 bytes (inb, inw or inl) according to bytes and calls pci_cfgdisable (which does nothing); for bytes other than 1, 2 and 4 nothing is read even if the port was valid. It then releases the mutex and returns the data, which is -1 when pci_cfgenable rejected the arguments or when bytes was not 1, 2 or 4. A 4-byte read can return any 32-bit value, which as an int may be negative. The caller must not hold pcicfg_mtx.
note: pcireg_cfgread at pci_cfgreg.c:193-216, read in full. Reviewers: original (a 4-byte read can return 32-bit values) right; round 1 (-1 also for bytes == 4 when pci_cfgenable fails) right.

name: ept_init
prose: Checks that the CPU's EPT/VPID capabilities (MSR_VMX_EPT_VPID_CAP) are sufficient for bhyve and sets the global nested-pmap flags; ipinum is the IPI number that is masked into the flags. It returns EINVAL, without changing ept_pmap_flags or ept_enable_ad_bits, if the capability lacks a 4-level page walk, write-back EPT memory type, INVVPID support with all types, or INVEPT support with all types. Otherwise it sets ept_pmap_flags to ipinum & PMAP_NESTED_IPIMASK, adds PMAP_PDE_SUPERPAGE when the tunable hw.vmm.ept.use_superpages (default 1) is set and the CPU supports 2 MB superpages, sets ept_enable_ad_bits to 1 when hw.vmm.ept.use_hw_ad_bits (default 1) is set and the CPU supports accessed/dirty bits (otherwise it adds PMAP_EMULATE_AD_BITS to the flags), adds PMAP_SUPPORTS_EXEC_ONLY when hw.vmm.ept.use_exec_only (default 1) is set and the CPU supports execute-only mappings, and returns 0.
note: ept_init at ept.c:76-118, read in full. The previous contract allowed only 0 or 22 (EINVAL is 22 on FreeBSD); contract removed because it names global state. Previous prose substantially matches.

name: vmcs_snapshot_any
prose: Saves or restores one VMCS field to or from a snapshot buffer: meta->op selects VM_SNAPSHOT_SAVE or VM_SNAPSHOT_RESTORE, ident names the field and running tells whether the vCPU is running; it returns 0 or an error number. For save it reads the field with vmcs_getany (returning its error if that fails) and then stores the value in the snapshot buffer with SNAPSHOT_VAR_OR_LEAVE, which sets ret to the macro's error and jumps to the exit if the buffer copy fails. For restore it first loads the value from the snapshot buffer with SNAPSHOT_VAR_OR_LEAVE (on failure it returns that error and does not write the VMCS) and then writes it with vmcs_setany, returning that call's error if non-zero. For any other meta->op it returns EINVAL. It returns the last value of ret.

Reviewers: original (the prose omitted the SNAPSHOT_VAR_OR_LEAVE error and the precondition excluded the EINVAL branch) right, 538-540 and 545-547; round 1 (on a restore buffer copy failure the code returns before vmcs_setany) right, 540-542; round 2 (the precondition forbids an invalid op yet the postcondition documents EINVAL) right. Tally 3 right.

name: ppt_setup_msix
prose: Sets up or tears down one MSI-X vector (idx) of a PCI passthrough device identified by (vm, bus, slot, func); addr and msg give the guest MSI address and data and vector_control the vector's control word. It takes PPT_LOCK itself and releases it before returning; it returns 0 or an error number. It returns the error from ppt_find if the device is not found, EBUSY if MSI (not MSI-X) is already in use, ENXIO if the device has no ivars, and for the first call on a device (no MSI-X set up yet) EINVAL if the device has no MSI-X vectors, ENOSPC (after ppt_teardown_msix) if the MSI-X table or PBA BAR resource cannot be allocated, and, if pci_alloc_msix fails, that function's error (or ENOSPC when it succeeded but allocated fewer vectors than requested), also after tearing down. It allocates the resource, cookie and argument arrays on that first call. It returns EINVAL if idx is out of range. If the vector's mask bit in vector_control is clear it tears down any existing interrupt for idx, allocates the IRQ resource (ENXIO if that fails), fills arg[idx] with the device, addr and msg and registers pptintr with bus_setup_intr (on failure it releases the resource and returns ENXIO); if the mask bit is set it only tears down the interrupt for idx. It returns 0 on those paths.

name: vatpit_update_mode
prose: Handles a write of the control byte val to the virtual i8254 PIT mode port (the caller holds the vatpit lock); it returns 0 or -1. It splits val into the select field (channel or read-back), the read/write field and the mode. If the select field is TIMER_SEL_READBACK it returns the result of pit_readback(vatpit, val), which latches counter or status values of the selected channels and so can change channel state. If the read/write field is neither TIMER_LATCH nor TIMER_16BIT it returns -1; if it is not TIMER_LATCH (a mode programming) and the mode is not one of TIMER_INTTC, TIMER_RATEGEN, TIMER_SQWAVE or TIMER_SWSTROBE it returns -1. Otherwise, for the channel selected by sel >> 6, a latch command updates the counter and latches it with pit_update_counter(vatpit, c, true), and a mode programming stores the mode in the channel, clears its output latch byte (olbyte) and sets TIMER_STS_NULLCNT in its status; then it returns 0.

Reviewers: original (the read-back dispatch returns whatever pit_readback returns, not -1) right, 307-308; round 2 (formal contract weaker than prose) moot, contract removed; round 15 (the read-back path changes channel state, contrary to "without changing any channel state") plausible but pit_readback was not read, so stated as possible. Tally 1 right.

name: vlapic_fire_lvt
prose: Delivers the local-vector-table interrupt lvt of the virtual local APIC vlapic to its vCPU and returns 1 if it was handled as an interrupt or 0 if nothing was delivered. It reads the last value written to the LVT entry (lvt_last[lvt]) with an acquire load. It returns 0 if the mask bit APIC_LVT_M is set. Otherwise it dispatches on the delivery mode: for fixed delivery a vector below 16 records a send-illegal-vector error in the ESR (vlapic_set_error, for the error LVT the flag is passed as such) and returns 0, otherwise vlapic_set_intr_ready is called and vcpu_notify_lapic only if that returned non-zero, and the function still returns 1 even when the interrupt was already pending and no notification was sent; NMI mode injects an NMI with vm_inject_nmi and returns 1; ExtINT mode injects an external interrupt with vm_inject_extint and returns 1; any other delivery mode is ignored and returns 0.
note: vlapic_fire_lvt at vlapic.c:441-473, read in full; vlapic_set_intr_ready and vlapic_set_error not read. Reviewers: original and round 15 (it returns 1 even when vlapic_set_intr_ready returns 0, so no vcpu_notify occurs) right, 459-460 and 472. Tally 2 right.

name: vrtc_time_update
prose: Updates the virtual RTC's base time to newtime with the host uptime base newbase; the caller holds the vrtc lock (asserted); it returns 0 or EBUSY. It saves the current alarm fields, always stores newbase in vrtc->base_uptime, and returns 0 at once if newtime equals the old base_rtctime. If newtime is VRTC_BROKEN_TIME it stores that in base_rtctime and returns 0. If the guest has halted RTC updates (rtc_halted) it returns EBUSY, leaving base_rtctime as it was (the base uptime has already been changed). Otherwise it advances base_rtctime toward newtime: when alarm interrupts are enabled and the old time was not VRTC_BROKEN_TIME it steps one second at a time, converting each second to RTC fields and setting the alarm interrupt flag in reg_c whenever the alarm fields match (values of 0xC0 or more are wildcards); in the other cases it sets base_rtctime to newtime directly. After the loop it sets the update-ended interrupt flag in reg_c if that interrupt is enabled, and returns 0.
note: vrtc_time_update at vrtc.c:417-491, read in full; rtc_halted and secs_to_rtc not read. Reviewers: original (omits the VRTC_BROKEN_TIME special case, which is handled before the halt check and sets base_rtctime directly) right, 446-449; round 15 (the one-second stepping also requires oldtime != VRTC_BROKEN_TIME) right, 467-470. Tally 2 right.

name: vrtc_set_reg_b
prose: Handles a guest write of newval to the virtual RTC's register B (the vrtc lock is held, asserted); it returns 0, or -1 in one case. It stores newval in reg_b and computes the changed bits. If the HALT bit changed: when HALT is being cleared it reads the guest-programmed time with rtc_to_secs and takes the current uptime as base, and if that time is VRTC_BROKEN_TIME and the tunable rtc_flag_broken_time is set it returns -1 (reg_b has already been updated); when HALT is being set it freezes the current time into the RTC fields (secs_to_rtc), sets the new time to VRTC_BROKEN_TIME and clears RTCSB_UINTR from reg_b (so reg_b can differ from newval). In both HALT cases it then calls vrtc_time_update with the new time and base (whose success is only asserted). If any interrupt-enable bit changed it recomputes reg_c with vrtc_set_reg_c. It then resets the periodic callout with vrtc_callout_reset when the frequency changed, and otherwise calls vrtc_callout_check, and returns 0.
note: vrtc_set_reg_b at vrtc.c:645-718, read in full; vrtc_time_update is at 417-491 (read above). Reviewers: original (reg_b is not simply set to newval because setting HALT clears RTCSB_UINTR) right, 691-692; round 15 (the -1 return happens only when HALT is being cleared, not for a HALT transition in general) right, 667-673. Tally 2 right.

name: vm_run
prose: Runs the guest vCPU vcpu until an exit that must be handled by user space or an error, and returns 0 or an error number. It returns EINVAL if the vCPU's id is not in the VM's active_cpus or is in suspended_cpus. Otherwise it loops: with a critical section entered it records the TSC, sets PCB_FULL_IRET, restores the guest FPU state, requires the vCPU state VCPU_RUNNING, runs the guest with vmmops_run, requires VCPU_FROZEN afterwards, saves the guest FPU state, adds the run time to the statistics and leaves the critical section. If vmmops_run returned 0 it sets retu to false, advances nextrip past the instruction and handles the exit code: request-idle, suspended, rendezvous, HLT, paging, instruction emulation, in/out and debug exits are passed to their handlers (which set the error and may set retu to request return to user space); IOAPIC EOI exits are processed; MONITOR, MWAIT and VMINSN exits inject #UD; any other exit code sets retu to true so user space handles it. Then, if there was no error and the exit code is VM_EXITCODE_IPI, vm_handle_ipi is called (it may set retu). If there is no error and retu is false it restarts the loop. Otherwise (a vmmops_run error, a handler error, or a request to return to user space) it increments VMEXIT_USERSPACE, logs and returns error, which is 0 when the exit is to be handled in user space.
note: vm_run at vmm.c:1123-1228, read in full; the exit handlers and vmmops_run not read. Reviewers: original (it returns 0 when retu is true, and a vmmops_run error returns without restart) right, 1170-1171 and 1221-1227; round 2 (omits the VM_EXITCODE_IPI handling through vm_handle_ipi; the default case sets retu to true) right, 1208-1219; round 15 (a nonzero vmmops_run result still increments VMEXIT_USERSPACE before returning) right, 1224. Tally 3 right.

name: emulate_movs
prose: Emulates one iteration of a MOVS (string move, opcode 0xA4 byte or 0xA5 word/dword/qword) instruction for a bhyve guest where one operand is memory-mapped I/O at gpa; the parameters are the vCPU, the decoded instruction vie, the guest paging state, the memread and memwrite callbacks and their argument. It uses opsize 1 for 0xA4 and vie->opsize otherwise. With a REP prefix it reads RCX and returns 0 immediately, doing nothing, when the count (masked to the address size) is 0. It translates the source address (segment override or DS, offset RSI) and, if the translation reports a guest fault or an error, jumps to done (returning the error, or 0 when only a fault was reported so that the guest resumes and takes the fault). If the source can be mapped with vm_copy_setup it reads the value from guest memory and writes it to the I/O address with memwrite (the source is ordinary memory and the destination is the MMIO location); otherwise it translates the destination (ES:RDI), and if that maps it reads the value from the I/O address with memread and copies it out; if neither side maps it translates both to guest-physical addresses and performs memread from the source followed by memwrite to the destination. A fault or error in any of these steps goes to done without updating registers. On success it adjusts RSI and RDI by opsize (decreasing when the direction flag is set, otherwise increasing), and for REP decrements RCX and, if it is still non-zero, calls vm_restart_instruction so that the instruction runs again. It returns 0 or EFAULT (asserted by a KASSERT at done); a guest page fault that must be reflected to the guest also returns 0 (fault is set), not EFAULT.
note: slice cut the head; the real function emulate_movs at vmm_instruction_emul.c:757-936, read in full; get_gla, vm_copy_setup and the register helpers not read. Reviewer round 15 (the vm_copy_setup fault path returns 0, not EFAULT) right, 819-823 and 932-935. Tally 1 right.

name: alpine_serdes_eth_mode_set
prose: Sets the SerDes group's Ethernet mode (SGMII or KR); group indexes the global alpine_serdes_eth_group_mode array, whose entry address is computed before the bounds check (the pointer arithmetic happens first, but the entry is only used after the check). It returns EINVAL without touching hardware if serdes_base is NULL or if group >= SERDES_NUM_GROUPS. Otherwise it locks the group's mutex; if the mode was not set before or differs from mode it initialises the group object with al_serdes_handle_grp_init, calls mode_set_sgmii for SGMII or mode_set_kr for any other mode value, and records the new mode and sets mode_set. It unlocks the mutex and returns 0.

name: bp_hardening_action
prose: Per-CPU action (arg unused) that calls handle_bp_hardening(disable_bp_hardening == 0), i.e. it asks for branch-predictor hardening to be enabled unless disable_bp_hardening is non-zero; it returns nothing. handle_bp_hardening (cpuinfo.c:384-490) for an ARM-implemented CPU selects BPIALL (with an ACTLR bit for the Cortex-A8; with no ACTLR bit for A9, A12, A17, A57, A72, A73 and A75) or ICIALLU (Cortex-A15, with ACTLR bit 0) through apply_bp_hardening; an unknown ARM part leaves the kind NONE and the global state unchanged; if apply_bp_hardening fails (the ACTLR bits cannot be written because firmware locked them) it sets the per-CPU kind to NONE, clears spectre_v2_safe and prints a warning; for a Qualcomm CPU or any other implementer it prints a warning (Qualcomm) and sets the per-CPU kind to NONE and spectre_v2_safe to 0; on the normal path it only prints the chosen kind when bootverbose. So enabling can fail or be a no-op, and the resulting state need not match disable_bp_hardening == 0.
note: bp_hardening_action at cpuinfo.c:505-509; handle_bp_hardening at 384-490 read, apply_bp_hardening not read. Reviewers: original (it may fail to enable, e.g. when ACTLR is locked, so the state need not match) right, 482-489; round 2 (the unknown-part and disable paths: an unknown ARM part leaves both unchanged, while other implementers set NONE and spectre_v2_safe 0) right, 442-443 and 477-479; round 15 (the QCOM path also changes state) right, 445-452 and 477-479. Tally 3 right.

name: pmap_preboot_get_vpages
prose: Early-boot allocator: allocates num pages of physical memory with pmap_preboot_get_pages (which returns last_paddr and advances it by num * PAGE_SIZE without any check), takes the next virtual range of the same size from virtual_avail (advancing virtual_avail by num * PAGE_SIZE), maps the pages at that address with pmap_preboot_map_pages, zero-fills the mapped range with bzero and returns the virtual address, which is the value virtual_avail had on entry.
note: pmap_preboot_get_vpages at pmap-v6.c:1025-1042 and pmap_preboot_get_pages at 731-739, read in full. Reviewer round 15 (the code only allocates and maps, it does not zero) wrong: bzero is at line 1039. Round 1 (formal omits the mapping and virtual_avail postconditions) right, contract removed. Tally 1 right 1 wrong.

name: sdma_configure
prose: Configures SDMA channel chn on the i.MX6 with the channel configuration conf and starts loading its context; it returns 0 on success or -1. It records conf in the channel, stops the channel (sdma_stop), sets the channel priority to 1, sets bit chn in the event-enable register for conf->event and clears the overrides. If conf->num_bd is greater than MAX_BD it prints an error and returns -1 before touching the buffer descriptors or the context. Otherwise it fills conf->num_bd buffer descriptors (command from conf, status BD_DONE | BD_EXTD | BD_CONT | BD_INTR with BD_WRAP added to the last, count conf->period, buffer address conf->saddr + conf->period * i), sets the channel control block's base and current BD pointers to the physical address of the channel's descriptors, builds a zeroed channel context (program counter from the firmware's mcu_2_app_addr, the event mask in gReg[0] or gReg[1] (conf->event above 32 uses gReg[0] with the event modulo 32), conf->daddr in gReg[6] and conf->word_length in gReg[7]), prepares buffer descriptor 0 to write that context into the SDMA data memory at the channel's offset, starts channel 0 with a write to SDMAARM_HSTART and returns 0 without waiting for or checking the context load (the wait loop is compiled out with #if 0).
note: slice cut the head; the real function sdma_configure at imx6_sdma.c:241-350, read in full. The old name "(unnamed) channel setup" is replaced by the real name; sdma_stop and sdma_overrides not read.
